explanation: Faithful to Szemerédi–Vu. There is an absolute C > 0 such that any A ⊆ ℕ with |A∩[1,N]| ≥ C√N for large N is subcomplete, meaning its finite subset sums contain an infinite AP a + kd with d > 0. The ∃C reading is the correct one: the 'for every implied constant' reading is false by Erdős' (2N)^{1/2} sharpness example. countUpTo counts [1,N] as on the page.
